If you mean using ASCII characters to make a C++ console interface, you can create boxes, headers, menus, and designs using characters like *, =, |, and ASCII codes.

Example: Simple MEDICODE Interface

C++
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int main() {

    cout << "========================================\n";
    cout << "              M E D I C O D E           \n";
    cout << "========================================\n";
    cout << "|                                      |\n";
    cout << "|         HEALTHCARE NAVIGATION         |\n";
    cout << "|                                      |\n";
    cout << "========================================\n\n";

    cout << "[1] Physical Health\n";
    cout << "[2] Mental Health\n";
    cout << "[3] Patient Profile\n";
    cout << "[4] Exit\n";

    return 0;
}

Output:

Plain text
======================================== M E D I C O D E ======================================== | | | HEALTHCARE NAVIGATION | | | ======================================== [1] Physical Health [2] Mental Health [3] Patient Profile [4] Exit

Using actual ASCII codes

You can also use char():

C++
cout << char(201); // ASCII/extended character
cout << char(205);
cout << char(187);

⚠️ But characters like ╔══╗ are usually extended ASCII/code-page characters, so they may not display correctly in every terminal.

For example, you can simply paste Unicode box characters:

C++
cout << "╔════════════════════════════╗\n";
cout << "║         MEDICODE           ║\n";
cout << "╠════════════════════════════╣\n";
cout << "║  1. Physical Health        ║\n";
cout << "║  2. Mental Health          ║\n";
cout << "║  3. Patient Profile        ║\n";
cout << "║  4. Exit                   ║\n";
cout << "╚════════════════════════════╝\n";

This looks cleaner for a console interface.

If you want, I can also make you a complete stylish ASCII interface for your MEDICODE C++ program with menus, borders, and colors.

Why your previous design looks broken

These characters:

Plain text
╔ ═ ╗ ║ ╚ ╝ █

are Unicode characters, not basic ASCII. Your terminal encoding is reading their UTF-8 bytes incorrectly, causing the Γé... symbols.

If you REALLY want the fancy design

Add this near the beginning of your main():

C++
SetConsoleOutputCP(CP_UTF8);

So:

C++
int main() {

    SetConsoleOutputCP(CP_UTF8);

    HANDLE hConsole = GetStdHandle(STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE);
